clue.text: Browning expert is good health professional

definitions.meaning: someone skilled at browning bread under the grill, a master of toast
the person at a formal dinner whose job is to call the toasts, raising glasses to everyone's good health

explanation.surface: A tanning specialist turns out to be a medical professional.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are whimsical readings of the same compound: a master of toast, and a professional proposer of toasts ('Good health!').
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses play on the two meanings of toast: grilled bread and a drink raised in someone's honour.

clue.text: This boat unwieldy? Objection overturned

indicators.note: turned over, so in this down clue the word for an objection is written upwards

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a clumsy boat is the issue, and an objection is overruled.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, broad, clumsy vessel is disparagingly called an old tub.

clue.text: Be a nuisance, wanting tea say not in a mug?

indicators.note: the letter for tea goes inside the words for a mug

parts.note: a mug is a drinking cup

indicators.note: as spoken, the drink tea is the letter T

parts.note: the drink named in the clue, said aloud

explanation.surface: A fussy guest kicks up because their tea isn't served in a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to take tea as the sound of the letter T; it sits inside A CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an idiom for misbehaving or causing trouble.

clue.text: Time to embrace many times over

parts.note: to embrace is to enfold in one's arms

explanation.surface: It's time for a hug repeated again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten times over is a lot, so the word is used loosely for greatly multiplied.

clue.text: Port Gabriel, for one

definitions.meaning: a Russian harbour city on the White Sea, also spelt Arkhangelsk
Gabriel is one of the chief angels of scripture, an example of the rank

explanation.surface: A harbour town named after the angel Gabriel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian White Sea port shares its name with the rank held by Gabriel among heavenly messengers.

clue.text: Italicise "Hard earth cultivated"

parts.note: italic type slopes, so to italicise is to tilt the letters
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An instruction to set a headline about farmed soil in italics.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is soil that has been tilled, its prepared and worked condition.

clue.text: Being in flight, not agree say to turn back for son

indicators.note: one piece stands in place of the son, replacing it

parts.note: to refuse is to decline or not agree
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'say' is written backwards

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing who would not agree to go back for their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn back' reverses EG to GE, and 'for son' puts GE where the S of REFUSE was.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fleeing persecution or war is someone in flight from their homeland.

clue.text: Renounce piece of meat

definitions.meaning: to give up or drop, as when one ... out sugar or ... ties
a butcher's joint, such as a prime rib portion

explanation.surface: Giving up a slab of steak, perhaps as a new vegetarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from slicing: severing a habit, and a slice of the carcass sold by a butcher.

clue.text: Place limits on prison transport

parts.note: cons, convicts, are a prison's inmates
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Restrict the vehicles that carry convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or hold within bounds.

clue.text: Various stuff in rear of loft — it hasn't had to be sorted

indicators.note: the final letter of loft goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of the phrase must be put into a new order
the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Junk at the back of the attic that nobody has got round to sorting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sorted' rearranges the ten letters of IT HASN'T HAD; 'rear of' gives T from loft, and 'in' places it among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase for miscellaneous odds and ends, assorted bits.

clue.text: Sort of garden abandoned to Caliban

indicators.note: let loose, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden left to Caliban, the wild islander of The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant collections displayed for study are kept in a garden of this kind, as at Kew.

clue.text: Moulds are amusing — man impressed

parts.note: fun means amusing, as in a fun evening
a GI is a US soldier, often a conscripted, that is impressed, man

explanation.surface: Someone finds mould funny and is impressed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' here means pressed into service, as old navies impressed sailors, describing the GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulds belong to the kingdom of mushrooms and yeasts.

clue.text: Live broadcast recommending a large jar

parts.note: AM is what 'live' means in 'I am'

indicators.note: spoken on air, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to be for something is to recommend it, so 'recommending a' gives FOR A, which spoken matches the jar's ending

explanation.surface: A radio advert endorsing a big jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' says that AM FOR A, spoken, gives the jar's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel.

clue.text: Roughly overturned sideboard brought round at house

indicators.note: turned over, so the abbreviation for roughly is read upwards

parts.note: CA, circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: the furniture word is wrapped round the little word 'at'

parts.note: a commode is a chest of drawers or sideboard

explanation.surface: Furniture movers tip over a sideboard and carry it into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To house someone is to put them up or provide lodging, a verb sense.

clue.text: Leader of group rowing sent to back area after hotel meal

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the hotel letter

parts.note: H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: the first letter of the rowing crew word is the one that moves
the leading letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A crew leader is banished to the rear after a hotel dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen; the clue's 'Leader of' and 'sent to back' are split around 'group rowing' but form one instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is an early-evening cooked meal with tea, traditional in Britain.

clue.text: Covered, having undergone a criminal check

definitions.meaning: enclosed in a box or sheath, as spectacles in a holder
of a building, reconnoitred by thieves before a robbery

explanation.surface: A building wrapped up after being vetted by burglars.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is sheathed or boxed; the other is underworld slang for scouting a target before a raid.

clue.text: Refuge from horrible scary aunt

indicators.note: something horrible is ugly and misshapen, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Escaping from a frightening relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctuary is a place of safety or shelter.

clue.text: The King's estate bringing honour to country

parts.note: grace is favour or honour, as in 'by the grace of God'
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A monarch's estate brings distinction to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, whose Memphis mansion bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis, called the King of rock and roll, lived at this Memphis mansion.

clue.text: One cat breaks away, almost — touch wood

indicators.note: the pieces break into the word for away, splitting it
the word for away loses its last letter

parts.note: absent means away, not present
I is the Roman numeral one
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A single cat escapes almost, so knock on wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ABSENT to ABSEN, and I + TOM 'breaks' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'may this omen be absent', said to avert ill luck.

clue.text: Europeans on moon altered particles, in theory

indicators.note: the Europeans are placed after the rearranged moon
changed, so the letters of moon are rearranged

parts.note: Poles are natives of Poland

explanation.surface: Europeans landing on a changed moon, theoretical physics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in theory' is fair because magnetic monopoles are predicted by physics but never yet detected.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists predict hypothetical magnetic objects with a single pole, not yet observed.

clue.text: In French town, dead level

indicators.note: the word for dead goes in the name of the town

parts.note: Pau is a town in south-west France
late means dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: Something dead in a French town, flat and level.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of level high ground.

clue.text: Poor people feel this secure at church

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten or secure it
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The poor feel safe in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'feel the pinch', to suffer financial hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Those short of money are said to feel the pinch of hardship.

clue.text: Dignitary could be said to be on time?

definitions.meaning: a high-ranking churchman, such as a bishop

definitions.text: could be said to be on time?
definitions.meaning: someone not yet late, before being late, is punctual

explanation.surface: A church dignitary might be called punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the word as PRE-LATE: before late, so on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric such as a bishop or archbishop holds this title; the joke reading is 'before late'.

clue.text: Withdraw in wrong order in remote country

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to back out is to withdraw

explanation.surface: A retreat in the wrong order through a remote land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in wrong order' swaps the halves of BACK OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian interior far from towns is called the bush or this name.

clue.text: Last of milk infant brought up, producing spit

indicators.note: 'last of' points at the closing letter of the word milk, the one that comes at its end
in a down clue, the infant word is written upwards

parts.note: a babe is an infant

explanation.surface: A baby brings up the last of its milk, spitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a baby's spit-up; 'spit' is the skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked on a skewer or spit.

clue.text: Racing home perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the British season of horse racing without jumps
a flat is an example of a home, an apartment

explanation.surface: Is this the home straight in racing?
explanation.definitionFit: Flat racing is called by this name in Britain, and a flat is an apartment.

clue.text: Flower, deep in the ground, no forget-me-not!

definitions.text: Flower, deep in the ground, no forget-me-not!

parts.words: Flower, deep in the ground, no forget-me-not!
parts.note: a flower is a river; this river of the underworld made the dead forget, so it is the opposite of a flower bidding remembrance

explanation.surface: A deep-planted bloom that is no forget-me-not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crosswordese for river; this one runs in Hades and its waters cause forgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, a river of the underworld whose waters caused oblivion.

clue.text: Fast one taking secretary in

indicators.note: the word for one takes another piece within it
the secretary sits inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A quick worker picks up a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means swiftly, at speed.

clue.text: High-flown weapon — nearly a cluster of them?

parts.note: a bomb is a weapon

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stick of bombs is a group dropped in a line from an aircraft

explanation.surface: Pompous language about a weapon and its cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to the weapon: a stick of bombs, trimmed by 'nearly' to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic speech is pompous, inflated rhetoric.

clue.text: Fish not bought on credit

definitions.meaning: a common white sea fish of the North Atlantic
cash on delivery, paid in full when goods arrive

explanation.surface: A fish paid for in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic white fish, and the abbreviation for cash on delivery.

clue.text: Fishy-sounding place

indicators.note: the word heard aloud gives the place name

parts.note: eely means like an eel, so fishy

explanation.surface: A town with a fishy name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England, historically famous for eels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is an English cathedral city, an example of a town.

clue.text: Second-hand story of Pope's toe?

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes
the toe is at the end of the leg

explanation.surface: A rumour about a pontiff's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toe' is read as LEG END, the end of a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern myth passed on as true, typically heard from a friend of a friend.
